title: Face-wheel drive with a crank slide
description: From the frame, determine whether rotor C turns and slide Y travels at the illustrated instant by tracing the selected face and the independent keyed crank.
question: Drive A CW. Determine C (spin) and Y (horizontal) at the shown instant.

answer.explanation: Drive A CW. At the tooth section the two rim tangents must coincide. The marked CW tangents agree. A positive, B positive. The clutch locks for CW input. Its brake holds the output when the clutch overruns. B positive, C positive. The solid key makes A and K rotate together. A positive, K positive. The top crank pin sweeps right under CW drive. The slot takes the transverse component along the horizontal slide. K positive, Y positive. The requested motion is CW / right (in listed output order).

options.label: A
options.explanation: C is CW, while this choice gives stationary. Y is right, while this choice gives stationary. The brake can hold C when B turns CCW. Treating that brake as a stop for Y ignores the separate solid key from A to K and the horizontal velocity of the upper pin.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Y is right, while this choice gives stationary. CW motion of C requires the clutch to engage. A stationary Y would require zero pin travel across its slot, but a clockwise crank carries its top pin horizontally at this instant.

options.label: C
options.explanation: C is CW, while this choice gives stationary. For C to stay still, B must turn CCW and overrun the CW-locking clutch. For Y to go right, the top pin on the keyed crank K must sweep to the right.

options.label: D
options.explanation: This tuple matches the derived motions. For C to turn CW, B must turn CW and engage the clutch. The solid key also turns K clockwise, sending its upper pin and the horizontal slide to the right.
